title: Conditions Calculated to Destroy
thesis: Article 6(c) of the Rome Statute prohibits inflicting on the group conditions of life calculated to bring about its physical destruction in whole or in part. Track 2 MAID applicants are disproportionately poor, female, and offered minimal housing or income support before being approved for death.

scenes.headline: Conditions Calculated to Destroy
scenes.subhead: Death is being offered where housing, income, and palliative care should be.

scenes.unit: of Track 2 MAID recipients reviewed reported poverty as a factor
scenes.context: Office of the Chief Coroner of Ontario — Vulnerability and MAiD analysis (2024). About one in three Track 2 recipients reviewed reported poverty as a contributing factor. Offers of housing or income support were minimal or absent in most files.

scenes.unit: of Ontario Track 2 recipients were women
scenes.context: Track 2 deaths skew female, poor, and isolated — the demographic profile most exposed to the housing crisis, gendered poverty, and long-term care failure. Ontario Chief Coroner series.

scenes.unit: Track 2 share in the lowest material-resources quintile (vs 20% population baseline)
scenes.context: Office of the Chief Coroner of Ontario, MAiD Death Review Committee — Marginalization Data Perspectives (companion to the 2024 Vulnerability Report). Track 2 recipients are over-represented in the lowest material-resources quintile.

scenes.unit: Track 2 share in the highest residential-instability quintile
scenes.context: Same Marginalization Data Perspectives report. Track 2 recipients are heavily over-represented in the highest residential-instability quintile relative to the 20% population baseline.

scenes.speaker: Office of the Chief Coroner of Ontario, MAiD Death Review Committee
scenes.quote: In a substantial subset of Track 2 cases reviewed, the Committee identified that the suffering driving the request was rooted in unmet social needs that the health and social care system had failed to address before the request for MAiD was approved.

scenes.unit: of Canadians who could benefit receive palliative care near end of life
scenes.context: Canadian Institute for Health Information and Health Canada estimates: fewer than three in ten who could benefit from palliative care receive it before death, while federal MAID provision counts have grown year over year since 2016.

scenes.headline: Why this is argued under Article 6(c)
scenes.body:
Article 6(c) covers conditions of life calculated to bring about physical destruction in whole or in part. The Ontario coroner series documents Track 2 cases where unmet poverty, housing, and care needs drove the request — while MAID remained available and funded.

This page does not invent composite charts. The numbers above come from the coroner marginalization reports, provincial MAID pages, and CIHI palliative access estimates. Film is atmosphere only.
